Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal Learned counsel for the appellant prays for withdrawal of I.A.
No.6293/2025, an application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C./Section 430 of BNSS for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of the appellant.
2. Accordingly, I.A. No. 6293/2025 is dismissed as withdrawn.
3. With the consent of both the parties, heard the matter finally at motion hearing stage.

4. This appeal under Section 374(2) of Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the appellant being aggrieved by the judgment dated 30.06.2022 passed NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21621 2 CRA-6881-2022 by the learned Special Judge, POCSO Act, 2012, Bijawar, District Chhatarpur (M.P.) in S.C. It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that the prosecutrix is major as admitted by school teacher Tijaiya Ahirwar (P.W.5), who also admitted to be a relative of the prosecutrix.
Prosecutrix (P.W.1) is a consenting party.
Thus, it is submitted that it is evident from the statement of the prosecutrix that she was a consenting party.
Attention is drawn towards the fact that prosecutrix herself had admitted that they were talking with each other on mobile phone.
A day before the incident, she had received a phone call from Hariram and he asked her to come to Chhatarpur where he had promised to meet her.
She had consented to this proposal and had met him at Chhatarpur.
She has admitted that Hariram had called her from Delhi and then from Jhansi.
He had come from Ladakh.

Thereafter, she admitted that instead of carrying her books in the school bag, she had carried her clothing and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21621 3 CRA-6881-2022 Rs.800/- which were given by her father alongwith her.

In paragraph 8 of her cross-examination, she admitted that Hariram and the prosecutrix were living at Delhi in one of the rooms of the chawl having 5-6 rooms with no attached toilet, in a comfortable atmosphere.
She used to prepare meals for herself and Hariram.
6. Thus, it is submitted that the statement of the prosecutrix that she was happily living at Delhi and had taken her own clothes in the school bag alongwith some money reflects her consent.
7. The grand-father of prosecutrix, P.W. 2 has admitted that prosecutrix was born on 15 August but he cannot say as to in which year her birth took place.
He has admitted that the prosecutrix and another person had left for their school on 04.08.2018 on their bicycle.
8. P.W. 3 is the father of the prosecutrix.
He has admitted that prosecutrix had gone to her school on 04.08.2018 but she did not return.
His father had recorded report against Hariram at Police Station Bijawar.
In cross-examination, he admits that the prosecutrix had returned back to her home on 11.08.2018.
He further admits that he has no idea about his own date of birth.
Then he said that he was born in 1983.
He lost his first wife in the year 2006.
There are two children from the first marriage.
He admits that at the time of death of his first wife, his younger son was 1 year of age and he also admitted that there are no children from second wife.
He had performed his second marriage in 2009.

9. Ajay Kumar Gupta (P.W. 4) is the Assistant Teacher, who has NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:21621 4 CRA-6881-2022 stated that Police has not made any enquiry with regard to the prosecutrix.
P.W. 5 another Assistant Teacher, has stated that in the certificate, Ex.P/7, date of birth of the prosecutrix is mentioned as 15.08.2003.
She had taken admission on 01.07.2008.

sentences.text: Thereafter, in cross-examination, he has stated that the prosecutrix and her father are known to him, inasmuch as grand-father of the prosecutrix is his co- brother in relationship.
He further stated that when prosecutrix was admitted in his school, at that time she was aged about 9-10 years.
Her parents were hesitant to send her to school but at his insistence prosecutrix was admitted in his school.

Thus, if this date of admission of 2008 is taken into consideration and the deposition of this witness that at the time of admission, she was 9-10 years of age, then date of birth of the prosecutrix will be somewhere of 1999 and this fact is further corroborated by the statements of this witness P.W. 5 that at the time of admission her age was reduced by 3-3&1/2 years.
10.
Dr. Sukrati Jain (P.W.14) in her deposition has admitted that there were no injury marks on the body or private parts of the prosecutrix.
Hymen was torn but had not ruptured on the external side.
Her secondary sexual characters were fully developed.
She admitted that she had not given any advice for conduct of X-ray etc. for age determination of the prosecutrix.

11. On the other hand, learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State supports the impugned judgment and submits that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21621 5 CRA-6881-2022 record of the case speaks against the appellant and, therefore, no indulgence be shown in the matter.

12. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
13.
When the aforesaid evidences are taken into consideration, then it is evident that P.W.5 has categorically stated that at his insistence, prosecutrix was admitted in his school.
He has also admitted that at the time of admission, she was 9-10 years of age.
He has given date of admission as 01.07.2008.
Thus, date of birth of the prosecutrix will fall somewhere in 1998-1999.

He has stated that family of the prosecutrix was shy of admitting her in the school because of she being over age but at his insistence she was admitted and her age was reduced from actual age by 3-3&1/2 years.
This evidence of P.W.5 has remained unrebutted.
Thus, it is evident that prosecution has failed to prove the age of the prosecutrix.

14. Conduct of the prosecutrix (P.W.1) as noted above that she was talking to the appellant on phone; she had gone to Chhatarpur as per the request of the appellant and then had travelled with appellant from Chhatarpur to Delhi; she stayed at Delhi in a shared accommodation with a common toilet; she did not narrate either about forceful sexual assault or violation of her privacy or being kidnapped by the appellant and on the contrary she stated that she had kept her clothes in her school bag instead of her books and had taken Rs.800/- alongwith her, reflects that she was a consenting party.

Since prosecution has failed to prove the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:21621 6 CRA-6881-2022 fact that prosecutrix was minor, mere positivity of DNA report is not sufficient circumstances.

15. Hon'ble Gujarat High Court in Premjibhai Bachubhai Khasiya vs. State of Gujrat, (2009) CriLJ 2888 has held that positive DNA report can be of great significance where there is supporting evidence, however, cannot be accepted in isolation that is as a sole piece of evidence to record conviction in rape cases.

16.

sentences.text: Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ranjit Sing Brahmajeet Sing Sharma vs. State of Maharashtra, (2005) 5 SCC 294 observed that "DNA evidence may have a great significance where there is supporting evidence, dependent, of course, on the strength of that evidence.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: .... in every case one has to put the DNA evidence in the context of the rest of the evidence and decide whether taken as a whole it does amount to prima facie case."

17. Thus when examined in the light of the judgment of Hon'ble the Supreme Court in Ranjit Singh Brahmajeet Singh Sharma (supra) then it is evident that mere positivity of the DNA is not sufficient,
if prosecution fails to prove that prosecutrix was minor and there could not have been any valid consent of the prosecutrix.

18. Thus, in view of such facts, when it is a case of consent and in absence of prosecution proving that prosecutrix was minor, conviction NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:21621 7 CRA-6881-2022 cannot be upheld.
19. Accordingly, the appeal is hereby allowed.

20. T h e judgment dated 30.06.2022 passed by the learned Special Judge, POCSO Act, 2012,
Bijawar, District Chhatarpur (M.P.) in S.C. No.29/2018 is set aside.
21. The appellant be released forthwith if not required in any other case.
22. The record of the Court below be sent back to the concerned Court along with copy of this judgment for information and compliance.
